pageCache.pageTitle: Careers Department Intent Statement – Woodlands Community College
pageCache.text:
Careers Department Intent Statement
All of our students are on a ‘careers learning journey’. Teachers, mentors and SLT are continuously offering students the opportunities to learn about a variety of career pathways and as well as developing their employability skills.
Students are challenged to learn to think about and reflect upon their experiences. They are encouraged to think about the benefits of everything they are taking part in across the whole curriculum and also outside of school and how this contributes to their personal development.
Through consistency and high-quality lessons, PR activities and inspirational assemblies students develop a greater understanding of their capabilities and will develop a positive sense of self-worth. They will be able to consider their personal branding and how they present themselves in a professional manner that will enable them to market themselves to future employers.
In year 7 students complete a Compass+ questionnaire, designed to measure and evaluate students’ prior knowledge around careers, with the responses used to plan for meaningful encounters with employers, further education and training providers. In year 9 students complete aspiration surveys to look at the encounters and careers-related opportunities they have had, designed to inspire them to consider their post-16 destinations and focus on the relevant qualifications and skills needed. This impacts their readiness to make informed options choices by the end of Year 9. In KS4 one-to-one appointments with a dedicated Careers Advisor, along with individual mentoring and Progress Review Meetings with senior staff, ensures students are supported in making well-informed post-16 choices. All students leave Woodlands with a planned destination college or vocational pathway.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head Teacher’s Welcome Message – Woodlands Community College
pageCache.text:
Mr Henderson Head Teacher
Dear parents & carers
I am delighted to welcome you to Woodlands Community College. Woodlands is a school of great diversity, energy and creativity but above all it is typified by a caring and supportive ethos. Our students enjoy school, the high quality education they receive, the first class facilities they enjoy in our state of the art buildings and the strong relationships they form with the amazing staff here. We are the first choice school for our community and we take great pride in this vital responsibility.
As a small 11 to 16 school we feel it is so important that every student feels welcomed and part of our learning journey. We are a community that believes in lifelong learning and personal achievement. Our aim is to ensure all students leave Woodlands successfully prepared and confident in exploring the next steps in their own journey.
Our motto is “Respect, Responsibility, Resilience”. This message underpins everything we do, from the engaging high quality lessons, the inspiring assemblies, to the massive range of exciting extracurricular visits and activities we run here, Woodlands will inspire you!
Every student here is challenged to achieve their best. We offer the best teaching, curriculum, support and facilities to help all children succeed. Every teacher and member of staff at Woodlands is determined to provide the highest standards for all students. In turn we expect and demand the highest standards from our students. We expect learners to work hard, attend well, behave impeccably and show the resilience and determination needed to succeed.
On behalf of the students, staff and governors of the school we welcome you to come and see for yourselves how great this school is. We are all intensely proud of Woodlands, of what it has achieved and what it will be; the most successful school in Southampton! It is my mission as the new Headteacher here to make that vision a reality and by working together with staff and students in this exciting and vibrant learning community we will achieve this. There is no limit to success!
“Respect, Responsibility, Resilience”.
Mr HendersonHead Teacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Parents and Guardians – Woodlands Community College
pageCache.text:
Parents and Guardians
Young people today are living in a rapidly changing world and so preparing our students for the challenges and opportunities out there is a vital aspect of their education. Woodlands Community College is committed to developing and arming each individual student with the most up to date research and knowledge as they progress through the different key stages.
A key element to aiding a student’s development is instilling the valuable ideals of responsibility and independence to forge their own paths forward. Working in partnership with parents, the Careers Department guides and supports students in an enthusiastic and professional relationship throughout their time at Woodlands Community College.
Get directly involved yourself! If you work for an employer who would be willing to support our careers education providing, be that through attending a Fair as an exhibitor, or being a practise interviewer, we would love to hear from you. Head over to the Employer page to find out more.
For support with helping your Child make the right decision please see our frequently asked questions page and https://www.parentalguidance.org.uk/applications-interviews for further post 16 guidance.

WOODLANDS CAREERS
Careers Information Advice and Guidance is available to all our students through the school Careers Co-ordinator, Miss Lombardo.
Miss Lombardo is based in her teaching classroom, room 203. She is in school every day of the week.
Her contact details are:
Email: gloria.lombardo@woodlands.southampton.sch.uk , Tel: 023 8046 3303
Careers can be described as everything that students, and key stakeholders, need to know, understand and be able to do to ensure young people are supported to make their best next step.

CAREERS GUIDANCE
At Woodlands we place a strong emphasis on ensuring that all of our students leave us with a secure post-16 plan.
Our extensive careers programme ensures that all students have careers education delivered through PSHE lessons throughout the year for all year groups, alongside a range of exciting careers-based events and visits. Please see our PSHE and careers overview on the website for more information relating to the variety of topics they will cover.
Every year 11 student has an academic mentor who works closely with you and your child to ensure that your child makes a sensible and well-informed decision about their post-16 plan.
The school also has a Careers Advisor, Vicky Hall, who works in school one day a week. By the end of the academic year, all year 10 students will have had the opportunity to meet with her to discuss their post-16 plan. Should students miss this appointment or require an additional one, this can be made available to them in Year 11.
We ensure that all Year 11 students are made fully aware of Open Evenings for all local colleges and external providers so that students can take up the opportunity to visit colleges and gather all the necessary information for them to make well-informed decisions about their futures. Students’ mentors support them in making online applications to colleges and providers and ensure students attend interviews once invited to do so.
We firmly believe that there is no greater inspiration for our students than learning about the journeys of people from our own local community. As a result, we are in the process of building an alumni community from which we can draw on the varied experiences of our former students. At Woodlands we place a strong emphasis on ensuring that all of our students leave us with a secure post-16 plan.
Our extensive careers programme ensures that all students have careers education delivered through PSHE lessons throughout the year for all year groups, alongside a range of exciting careers-based events. Please see our PSHE and careers overview on the website for more information relating to the variety of topics they will cover.
If you are a former Woodlands student with a story to tell, words of advice or potential recruitment possibilities, please join our alumni and help us in our journey to inspire and educate our learners about the many wonderful possibilities available to them once they enter the world of work.
Our Careers provision is measured against the Gatsby Benchmarks and the impact is evaluated through pupil evaluations and measured through a post-16 tracking system.
If you have any queries relating to careers, please do not hesitate to contact our careers leader, Miss G Lombardo, at: gloria.lombardo@woodlands.southampton.sch.uk or call 02380 463303.

EMPLOYERS and RECRUITERS
The support of our local community is key to the Careers Education that Woodlands Community College School is aiming to provide. We are so lucky to have the backing of so many willing and enthusiastic employers, keen to get involved with our school calendar of activities every year. Sharing career experiences and providing opportunities to develop employability skills is invaluable to a young person’s progression and we cannot thank our existing partners enough.
Do you work in a business that could help provide work experience or opportunities for our students?
We are always looking for local businesses that are wanting to inspire and educate our students about the world of work and expand and develop our careers programme. If you think you could help us with practice interviews, talks/presentations to students, provide invaluable work experience or any other opportunities that give students the chance to develop core skills and motivation, please contact our Careers Co-ordinator– Miss Lombardo at gloria.lombardo@woodlands.southampton.sch.uk
If you’re an employer and are curious about how you could get involved, we would love to hear from you! There are many ways you could contribute to the Woodlands community and we are always open to new ideas and opportunities.
Please get in touch!

Labour Market Information
It is important for every student, parent and carer to be aware of and make use of Labour Market Information. This can help to prepare students for decisions on future study and potential job sectors. LMI is updated regularly and shows trends and opportunities to support students in a successful future career.
Complete the quizzes to discover real time jobs in the local area – Career Coach and Career Pilot.

Access Southampton Jobs Bulletin – local job updates, volunteering opportunities, and work experience listings. https://access-southampton.co.uk/jobs-bulletin
National Careers Service – the main UK careers site with job profiles, CV writing support, skills assessments, and advice. https://nationalcareers.service.gov.uk
National Apprenticeships Service – the official apprenticeship site where students can register and apply for vacancies. https://www.apprenticeships.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Clerk to Governors – Woodlands Community College
pageCache.text:
Clerk to Governors
Permanent, Part Time – Approximately 80 hours per year £17.00 per hour
Are you an enthusiastic and committed individual with great organisational and communication skills? If so, and you’re looking for a job with flexible, part time hours, then this could be an excellent role for you!
This is a rewarding and challenging role that will give you the opportunity to support governors to deliver the best outcomes for the pupils at Woodlands. You will administer and minute meetings, and any extra-ordinary meetings called by either the school or governors; these are mainly held in the evening. You will advise on governance legislation and policies following appropriate training.
You must be able to work under your own initiative, manage deadlines and maintain accurate records. The ability to remain impartial, comply with data protection legislation and maintain confidentiality is essential. The role is home and school based with the flexibility to complete clerking tasks around your existing commitments. There is a requirement to travel to Woodlands to clerk their governance meetings, we hold our governor meetings every half term.
We offer full training for the successful candidate and line management by the Chair of Governors.
Download an application form and job description from
www.woodlands.southampton.sch.uk
Please email your application to recruitment@woodlands.southampton.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and Inclusion – Woodlands Community College
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) and Inclusion
Special educational needs, also known as special educational needs and disabilities in the United Kingdom refers to the education of children who require different education provision to the mainstream system.
At Woodlands, we pride ourselves on being an inclusive school.
We have high aspirations for all our pupils, including those with SEND. We work closely with our feeder schools to ensure a smooth transition from Year 6 to 7 and also collaborate with post-16 providers to support transition into further education.
Pupils who have identified SEND will be supported through a variety of ways dependent on the level of need they present with. Class teachers monitor pupils through out the year and liaise closely with the SENDCos to ensure that any previously unidentified needs may be acknowledged and supported. At Woodlands, we ensure that we always strive to meet a pupil’s presenting need whether they have a diagnosis or not. We work closely with parents and outside agencies to ensure that we are providing support that will be enable pupils to make good progress from their starting points.
If you have any concerns about your child or would like to discuss anything further please contact the relevant key stage SENDCo:
Year 7, 8 and 9 – Sue Mendham sue.mendham@woodlands.southampton.sch.uk
Year 10 and 11- Emma Sinnett emma.sinnett@woodlands.southampton.sch.uk

How will we support parents to become part of the Woodlands Community?
Your first child joining secondary school is a big milestone for the whole family, and we understand that there may be many questions that parents have about the process. We have a number of ways to support parents at this crucial time too.
Class of 2031 Parent Facebook Group
All parents of students joining us in September are encouraged to join our Facebook group. This can be found via the “Groups” tab on the main Woodlands Facebook page once the places for September 2026 are released in March. This group is a really useful way to support one another, but also to ask questions and find key information. The group is overseen by Miss Sutton, one of our Deputy Headteachers, so there is always someone on hand to help with any queries.
Welcome Event for Families new to the Woodlands Community
If this is your first child to attend Woodlands, we would like to welcome you to the community with an informal “Coffee and Cake” event after school. The date for this will be sent to you as soon as places for September 2026 have been offered in March. This will simply be a chance to meet key staff, find out a little more about the transition process, especially our transition week, and ask any questions about your child’s particular needs.
We will hold a formal induction evening for all parents and students during Transition Week. This will help you find out more about our school, our expectations and our ethos, as well as being an important opportunity to meet key members of staff and try on school uniform. We would encourage all families to attend this event, on Wednesday 1st July and ensure that they have all the information they need for their child to start with us in September. This will take place on Wednesday 1st July for the Class of 2031.
Transtion
All students in the Class of 2031 will be invited to join us at Woodlands for a whole week from Monday 29th June to Friday 3rd July. This will be a fantastic opportunity for children to spend the whole week learning what it is like to be a Woodlands student; taking part in lessons and other activities; and most importantly, making new friends!
You will find more information about Transition Week in the letter sent home, but please mark this exciting event on your calendar.
Please ensure that you have completed the Transition Week Information Form here: https://forms.gle/JrP1cRXfQk2TWDd39
This is essential so that we can provide the correct support for your child.

Vision Statement
We will students of all abilities to be the best that they can be in all areas of school life, with a curriculum that is underpinned by a focus on the school values of Respect, Responsibility and Resilience.
We will provide our students with high quality learning experiences that will support them in raising their aspirations and develop the study skills that will enable them to have a wider range of future choices.
The school curriculum encompasses all learning opportunities within school life, including extra-curricular activities and development of the wider social skills that will prepare our students to take their place as active citizens in society.
